thread.title: Apple, iPhone suppliers lead major Silicon Valley stocks selloff

author: Marlize van Romburgh
title: Apple, iPhone suppliers lead major Silicon Valley stocks selloff
text: – Managing Editor, Silicon Valley Business Journal Nov 12, 2018, 1:31pm PST Updated Nov 12, 2018, 1:37pm PST The Dow Jones Industrial Average plummeted 600 points on Monday after Apple shares fell on worries of softening iPhone demand. Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL) shares fell 5 percent after one of its suppliers, Milpitas-based Lumentum Holdings, unexpectedlycut its second-quarter forecast . Shares of Lumentum (NASDAQ: LITE), which makes 3D sensors used for facial recognition in Apple’s latest iPhones, plummeted 33 percent Monday. U.S. stock markets were also rattled by a rise in the U.S. dollar and renewed trade war concerns . The Bloomberg Silicon Valley High Technology index of the region's largest tech stocks fell 3.8 percent on Monday, dragged down by Apple, Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD), down 8.8 percent; Applied Materials (NASDAQ: AMAT), down 4.4 percent; HP Inc. (NYSE: HPQ), down 3.8 percent; and Adobe Systems (NASDAQ: ADBE), down 3.2 percent. Cisco Systems (NASDAQ: CSCO) fell 2.9 percent, followed by Intel Corp. (NASDAQ: INTC), down 2.7 percent. Oracle Corp. (NYSE: ORCL)fell 2.6 percent. Google parent Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOG) and Facebook (NASDAQ: FB) dipped 2.4 percent and 2.2 percent, respectively, rounding out the Silicon Valley index’s worst performers for the day. Overall, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite index fell 2.7 percent. Other Silicon Valley stocks that posted big declines Monday were: Viavi Solutions Inc. (NASDAQ: VIAV) — down 11.7 percent Synaptics Inc. (NASDAQ: SYNA) — down 8.2 percent Align Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: ALGN) — down 7.9 percent Nvidia Corp.
